prompt: Write part of a deposition transcript (about 400 words) of a plaintiff in a car accident lawsuit. The defense lawyer asks (lines start with 'Q:') and the plaintiff answers (lines start with 'A:'). Accident: rear-end collision in Pearland, Texas. Injury: wrist fracture. Ask about the accident, treatment and daily life. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1364; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather not give my full name on the record yet. I'm the plaintiff in this case, and my attorney has asked that we keep personal details limited to what's needed.

Q: Your attorney can object if necessary. Let's move on. Where were you on the day of the collision?
A: I was driving home from work on a weekday afternoon. I was in the right lane on a main road in Pearland, Texas, heading toward my neighborhood.

Q: What was the traffic like?
A: It was moderate. Traffic was slowing down ahead of a light, and I came to a stop behind a pickup truck. I had my foot on the brake and my hands on the wheel.

Q: Did you see the vehicle behind you?
A: I checked my mirror just before I stopped, and I saw a sedan coming up quickly. I braced myself, but there was no time to do anything else.

Q: Describe the impact.
A: It was a hard hit from behind. My head snapped forward and back, and my car lurched into the truck in front of me. My right hand came off the wheel and hit the console. Right away I felt a sharp pain in my wrist.

Q: What did you do after the collision?
A: I stayed in the car for a few minutes because I was shaken up. Then a police officer came to the scene. Someone called an ambulance, and I was taken to the emergency room.

Q: What was the diagnosis?
A: The doctors said I had a fracture in my wrist. They put me in a splint and told me I would need a cast and follow-up visits with an orthopedic specialist.

Q: What treatment have you received since then?
A: I've had several follow-up appointments, physical therapy twice a week, and a second set of X-rays to check the healing. I still do exercises at home every evening.

Q: How has the injury affected your daily life?
A: Simple things are hard. I can't open jars easily, I had to stop cooking most of my meals, and I needed help washing my hair for several weeks. I also haven't been able to go back to my full schedule at work.

Q: Have you had any hobbies you stopped doing?
A: Yes. I used to play recreational volleyball on weekends and garden. I haven't been able to do either since the accident, and I miss them a lot.

Q: Do you still have pain today?
A: Yes, especially when the weather changes or when I grip something for a long time. Some days it aches for hours afterward.
